title: New Zealand Thrash India 5-0 in Auckland in First Friendly
excerpt: An early Bijoy Varghese own goal, a Jesse Randall brace, and second-half goals from Chris Wood and Lachlan Bayliss gave New Zealand a 5-0 win in the opening match of India's New Zealand tour; the sides meet again in Christchurch on Sunday.
body:
• New Zealand beat India 5-0 in their FIFA international friendly at Go Media Stadium, Auckland, on Thursday, November 12, 2026 — what the AIFF match report described as India's first-ever match in New Zealand.
  • Bijoy Varghese's fifth-minute own goal opened the scoring; Jesse Randall scored twice to make it 3-0 by half-time, Chris Wood headed the fourth in the 57th minute and Lachlan Bayliss volleyed the fifth in the 74th.
  • Goalkeeper Vishal Kaith saved a late penalty to keep the margin at five, on a night when India, ranked 138th, faced a New Zealand side ranked 88th that played at the 2026 World Cup.
  • What's next: the two teams meet again on Sunday, November 15, at One New Zealand Stadium in Christchurch, in the second friendly of the window.

India lost 5-0 to New Zealand in the first friendly of the November window at Go Media Stadium in Auckland on Thursday, in what the AIFF match report described as the Blue Tigers' first-ever match in New Zealand. Jesse Randall struck a brace, while Chris Wood and Lachlan Bayliss also found the net after a Bijoy Varghese own goal opened the scoring, the AIFF match report carried by Khel Now said.

How the match ran away

The afternoon went wrong almost immediately. In the fifth minute Varghese turned the ball into his own net, and Randall's two first-half goals left India trailing 3-0 at half-time. Wood netted the fourth from a header in the 57th minute before Bayliss volleyed in the fifth in the 74th, The Away End reported. The hosts also earned a late penalty that could have made it six, but Vishal Kaith saved it.

Head coach Khalid Jamil had picked a changed squad for the tour and left Gurpreet Singh Sandhu out. India lined up with Kaith in goal; Abhishek Singh Tekcham, Pramveer, Varghese and Akash Mishra in defence; captain Anirudh Thapa, Manvir Singh, Ryan Williams, Jithin MS, Liston Colaco and Lalremtluanga Fanai ahead of them, with six substitutions made across the second half.

What it means

The result was New Zealand's biggest victory against opposition from outside Oceania in 45 years, MyKhel reported. For India, it extended a difficult run in friendlies against World Cup-level opposition: across recent matches against Panama, Brazil, Uruguay and now New Zealand, India have scored twice and conceded 16. The gap in the rankings — New Zealand 88th, India 138th — was visible throughout.

For New Zealand, the match was the side's first appearance in front of home supporters since the 2026 FIFA World Cup, and one of Darren Bazeley's final matches as national team head coach, the Oceania Football Center reported. Randall's brace continued his goalscoring form for the All Whites in a performance their player ratings also marked as the night's standout.

What's next

Jamil has three days to find a response. The teams meet again on Sunday, November 15, at One New Zealand Stadium in Christchurch, closing India's November window.
